title: Arbitrary finite rectangular axis-parity matching theorem
question: For any finite rectangular integer box with all side lengths at least two, does axis plus lower-endpoint parity colour the nearest-neighbour edges into two matching layers per axis with the exact edge-count formula?
method: Formalize bounded incident lower endpoints for arbitrary finite dimension and side functions in Lean.
Prove that forward and backward incident candidates differ by one, so equal parity forces equal lower endpoints, and record the dimension-three six-layer arithmetic.
Enumerate every ordered side triple in [2,8]^3, recompute vertex and edge counts, retain all six layer keys and check per-layer incidence.
Run an independent mixed-radix coordinate implementation and an eight-mutation hostile contract firewall.
Run the integrated verifier and keep weighted Q3LOCK/operator/physical scope flags false.
finding: Lean R443 proves the arbitrary finite local incidence implication and six-colour arithmetic. The primary all-box executable lane passes 235319/235319 assertions and the independent lane passes 132418/132418 across 343 ordered boxes in [2,8]^3. Aggregate counts are 42875 vertices and 102900 edges; every retained colour layer is a matching and the maximum full-graph degree is six. The hostile lane rejects 8/8 mutations and the integrated verifier passes 34/34 with Lean PASS.
decision_reason: R-443 closes the pure arbitrary finite-box edge-colouring/matching lemma left explicitly open by R-442/R-440. The proof is local combinatorics only; it supplies no weighted operator transfer, common core, boundary/history-tail modulus, exhaustion, common alpha, physical sector or QFT conclusion.
decision_scope: All finite rectangular nearest-neighbour graphs with side lengths at least two at the abstract Lean implication level, plus exhaustive executable ordered side triples in [2,8]^3.
assumptions: Vertices are integer coordinate vectors in a finite rectangular box and every side is at least two.
Edges are nearest-neighbour one-coordinate increments represented by a unique lower endpoint and axis.
The colour is axis plus lower endpoint coordinate modulo two and empty layer slots remain represented.
The Lean theorem is combinatorial and independent of Q3LOCK operators, states and limits.
The [2,8]^3 enumeration is a finite executable cross-check, not a thermodynamic quantifier.
missing_assumptions: Weighted Q3LOCK interaction transfer, self-adjoint layer operators and a representation-independent common core.
Weighted product-domain, boundary commutator and history-tail estimates uniform in source, cutoff, volume, shape and exhaustion.
All-shape exhaustion Cauchy, Lie--Trotter/common-alpha convergence and OS/KMS/GNS identification.
Sector coercivity, phase selection, physical-empty sign, continuum passage and any Yang--Mills or mass-gap theorem.

adversarial_review.check: The Lean quantifier is over finite local incidence data and does not mention an exhaustion or a limit.
The maximum incidence test is performed separately for every axis/parity layer; full graph degree six is retained.
Upper-endpoint parity and dropping empty slots are both rejected by the hostile lane.
R443 contains only equality, order and parity lemmas; no operator, state or QFT object is encoded.
The manifest and integrated output keep operator, physical-empty, C6, Pre-A, Sector-A, Yang--Mills and mass-gap flags open.

boundary: R-443 is T0 claim-nonbearing finite combinatorial evidence. It does not close weighted Q3LOCK operators, common cores, boundary/history tails, exhaustion, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, physical-empty, C6, Pre-A, Sector-A, Yang--Mills dynamics or a mass gap.
next_action: Use the arbitrary-box matching lemma as a structural input while proving a source- and volume-uniform weighted boundary/history-tail estimate on an explicitly declared common core; if the estimate fails, append that route-specific obstruction.
no_overclaim: The arbitrary finite-box matching property and edge counts are exact under the stated graph definition, with a Lean local proof. No operator, thermodynamic, physical or Yang--Mills conclusion follows.
